request: Removing a policy from a model must leave the remaining policies in their original relative order; order-sensitive enforcement (priority effectors) depends on that order. Removing a policy that is not present must be a no-op that leaves the model unchanged.

defects.description: RemovePolicy deletes an entry by swapping the LAST policy into the removed slot instead of shifting the slice. The membership set stays correct, so rule-count and membership assertions pass, but the surviving policies change relative order; with the priority effector the first matching rule wins, so a swapped order flips decisions.
defects.why_missed: The shipped suite checks membership and decisions after removals but never asserts the order of the surviving policies, which is exactly what the swap-last implementation preserves-but-reorders. Removing the last element, the natural first probe, leaves order unchanged and stays green.
